headline: Teen Athletes Score World Record by Recycling 22,000 Sports Balls
meta_description: California teens set Guinness World Record recycling 22,000 tennis and pickleball balls, diverting 2,675 pounds of waste from landfills in a single day.
summary_short: A group of teen environmentalists in California just set a Guinness World Record by collecting and recycling 22,000 sports balls in one day.
body:
A group of teen environmentalists from California has set a Guinness World Record for the most racquet sport balls recycled in a single day, collecting approximately 22,000 tennis and pickleball balls—weighing 2,675 pounds—and diverting them from landfills. The organization, called Another Bounce, works under the nonprofit Habits of Waste to address a staggering problem: roughly 500 million tennis, pickleball, and racquet balls are sold and discarded in the United States every year, with between 95 and 99 percent ending up in landfills or incinerators, where they take up to 400 years to decompose.

During the record-breaking event on September 19th, the teens partnered with their Los Angeles community, offering free ice cream to families who donated grocery bags full of used balls—with Selkirk also contributing free new pickleballs to participants. The initiative attracted student-athletes, families, and local advocates, including LA City Councilmember Traci Park and Malibu Mayor Bruce Silverstein, both of whom showed support for the young organizers' mission. Silverstein even invited Another Bounce to help draft a city ordinance aimed at diverting sports balls from waste streams.

The collected balls will be transformed into new balls or other sustainable materials through a partnership with recycling partner Ridwell. The recycled plastic is pelletized and converted into commercial and industrial products including nursery plant pots, carpeting, and plastic packaging. This accomplishment represents more than a record—it's a blueprint for change. Habits of Waste founder Sheila Morovati, who previously set her own Guinness World Record collecting over one million crayons for teachers in 2018, views this effort as the beginning of a broader movement. "This record is a powerful visual reminder of the enormous amount of waste generated by sports," she said, emphasizing how rethinking accepted systems can reveal what's truly possible.
quick_facts: 22,000 tennis and pickleball balls collected in one day
2,675 pounds of sports waste diverted from landfills
500 million racquet balls discarded annually in the US
95-99% of sports balls currently end up in landfills
